summary: Shanghai Jiao Tong University admits international students to master's and doctoral programmes taught in Chinese or entirely in English, with scholarships by level. The scholarships are the Chinese Government Scholarship (CGS), the Shanghai Government Scholarship, the SJTU Scholarship, the SJTU Tuition Waiver Scholarship (master's), the SJTU Fellowship (doctoral) and school scholarships (master's). Applicants use the university's online application system and choose one scholarship channel only. The application fee is RMB 800.
eligibility_notes:
Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens holding a foreign ordinary passport for private purposes. Chinese nationality is decided by China's exit and entry authorities; if an applicant is found to hold Chinese nationality or not to meet the rules at any stage, the university can withdraw eligibility, the offer, enrolment or student status.

Applicants must be of good character, in good physical and mental health, meet the medical examination requirements, have a friendly attitude toward China, be willing to follow Chinese law and university rules, and have no criminal record or record of other violations.

Master's applicants need a degree equivalent to a Chinese bachelor's; doctoral applicants need a degree equivalent to a Chinese master's. Final-year students may apply with a certificate of expected graduation and must have the degree before registration and enrolment. Some schools accept bachelor's holders for direct entry to doctoral study.

Language: applicants must meet the Chinese or English proficiency rules in the university's language requirements document. English-taught programmes accept GRE (total 320; Verbal 160; Quantitative 160; Analytical Writing 3.5), GMAT (total 550; Verbal 25; Quantitative 35; Analytical Writing 4.0), IELTS Academic (overall 6.0, each component 5.5), TOEFL (tests before January 2026: overall 85, Reading, Listening and Speaking 20 each, Writing 22; tests from January 2026 on the new scale: overall 4, Reading 4, Listening 4.5, Speaking 4, Writing 4.5), Cambridge C1 Advanced (overall 176, each component 169) or Cambridge C2 Proficiency (180 and 180). Scores must be valid on the application date (two years for TOEFL and IELTS, five years for GRE and GMAT). Previous education in English can replace a test if it was completed within two years before applying, in English, in one of the listed English-speaking countries or regions, with a letter or certificate from the institution. Chinese-taught programmes need HSK 5 (total 200, each part 60) or HSK 6 (total 180, each part 60), or previous Chinese-medium education; most Chinese-taught science and engineering programmes also need English proficiency. Some programmes have their own rules (humanities master's: HSK 6 total 180; IMBA: IELTS 5.5 or TOEFL 90; Foreign Languages and French-taught programmes have separate tests).

Scholarship applicants must meet the admission rules, must not receive any other scholarship funding, and must be no older than 40 (doctoral) or 35 (master's). Self-funded applicants are also accepted.
age_experience_notes: For scholarships: doctoral applicants no older than 40, master's applicants no older than 35. No age limit is stated for self-funded applicants and no work-experience requirement is stated. Sixteen schools and institutes (master's) and twenty-five (doctoral) require a Letter of Intent for Supervision from an SJTU supervisor before applying.
funding_summary: Awards differ by scholarship and level and amounts are shown in the application system, not in the guide. Doctoral SJTU Scholarship: monthly stipend, tuition waiver, group comprehensive insurance in China and a partial accommodation subsidy. Master's SJTU Scholarship: monthly stipend, standard tuition waiver, group insurance and partial accommodation subsidy. Master's Tuition Waiver Scholarship: standard tuition waiver and group insurance. The SJTU Scholarship, Tuition Waiver Scholarship and School Scholarships may cover all or part of tuition, as set in the funding package confirmed by the university or school. Funding periods are not normally extended and recipients go through an annual review. CGS review and payment follow the rules of the authorities that administer it.
programmes_note: The 2027 catalogues list English-taught master's programmes (2 to 3 years) and doctoral programmes (4 years) by school, with major code, research fields, duration, tuition and contact. The doctoral catalogue includes programmes such as civil, mechanical, electrical, computer and materials engineering, mathematics, physics, biology, chemistry, public administration, foreign languages, law (S.J.D.), journalism and design; the master's catalogue also includes MIB, IMBA, finance, law (LL.M.), media, environmental science and the French-taught programmes of the SJTU Paris Elite Institute of Technology. The first 25 master's and 25 doctoral names (in catalogue order) are listed here; Chinese-taught catalogues are separate PDFs that were not read. Programme names, codes and tuition are in the catalogues linked as the catalogue source.
institutions_note: Single host university: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, which teaches at its Xuhui, Minhang, Huangpu, Changning, Pudong and Chongming campuses. Schools involved include Ocean and Civil Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation and Intelligent Sensing, Computer Science, Integrated Circuits, Materials Science and Engineering, Mathematical Sciences, Physics and Astronomy, Life Sciences and Biotechnology, Biomedical Engineering, Humanities, Antai College of Economics and Management, International and Public Affairs, Foreign Languages and others. Contact for admissions: International Affairs Office, Graduate School.

summary.detail: Master's programmes normally take two to three years, taught in Chinese or entirely in English. Applicants need a degree equivalent to a Chinese bachelor's (final-year students may apply with an expected-graduation certificate and must hold the degree before registration). Scholarship applicants must be no older than 35. Master's scholarships: Government Scholarships, SJTU Scholarships, SJTU Tuition Waiver Scholarships and School Scholarships. Sixteen schools and institutes require a Letter of Intent for Supervision from an SJTU supervisor before applying (Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Integrated Circuits, Materials Science and Engineering, Mathematical Sciences, Life Sciences and Biotechnology, Biomedical Engineering, Agriculture and Biology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Tsung-Dao Lee Institute, SJTU Paris Elite Institute of Technology, College of Smart Energy, Oceanography, Psychology, Ocean and Civil Engineering, Medicine). Tuition without a waiver is listed per programme in the catalogue (for example RMB 80,000 per year for most engineering and science programmes shown).

summary.detail: Doctoral programmes normally take four years, taught in Chinese or entirely in English. Applicants need a degree equivalent to a Chinese master's; some schools accept bachelor's holders for direct entry to doctoral study (see each school's announcement and catalogue). Scholarship applicants must be no older than 40. Doctoral scholarships: SJTU Fellowship, Government Scholarships and SJTU Scholarships. Doctoral applicants also upload a brief account of their research experience. Twenty-five schools and institutes require a Letter of Intent for Supervision before applying. Tuition without a waiver is listed per programme in the catalogue; most programmes shown are RMB 89,000 per year, a few RMB 90,000 or 100,000.

benefits.limit_text: Partial accommodation subsidy under the SJTU Scholarship; allowances are given according to the award level
benefits.conditions: Students may reserve on-campus accommodation or arrange their own off campus. The SJTU page for CGS says there is no free dormitory (stated there for undergraduates) and an undergraduate subsidy of CNY 1,100 per month; no graduate figure is stated.

benefits.conditions: CGS annual review and payment follow the rules of the authorities that administer it. Applicants not nominated for CGS are automatically considered for the Shanghai Government and SJTU Scholarships. The Shanghai Government Scholarship needs no separate application.

requirements.text: Original degree certificate(s): bachelor's for master's applicants; master's and bachelor's for doctoral applicants. Degrees from outside mainland China normally need a degree verification report from CSCSE; mainland China degrees need a CHSI verification report. Final-year students may first submit an official certificate of expected graduation and give the degree certificate and verification report before enrolment; graduates submit the report with the application.

Authentic and complete transcripts: undergraduate for master's applicants; undergraduate and master's for doctoral applicants. Final-year students submit current transcripts and give final ones before enrolment. If the grade point average is not shown, an official GPA statement from the university is also needed.
Proof of English or Chinese proficiency as set in the language requirements document (test report or evidence of previous education in that language).
Scan of the biographical page of a foreign ordinary passport for private purposes, valid for at least 12 months from the expected enrolment date (September 2027).
ID photo in JPG format, under 200 KB, at least 295 pixels wide and 413 pixels high.
Personal statement and research plan; doctoral applicants also upload a brief account of their research experience.
Two letters of recommendation from academics of associate professor rank or above (or equivalent), or senior professionals in a relevant industry.
Letter of Intent for Supervision from an SJTU supervisor, obtained before applying and following the school's own requirements.
requirements.conditional_rule: Only for the schools and institutes named in the guide (16 for master's, 25 for doctoral)

requirements.text: All uploaded documents must be original certificates in Chinese or English (otherwise with a notarised translation into English or Chinese) and scanned in colour with a scanner; phone photos and photocopies are not accepted. RMB 800 non-refundable application fee paid online.

application_steps.title: Choose your programme and check language, supervisor and age rules
application_steps.detail: Pick a programme from the 2027 English or Chinese catalogue and check its language test, tuition and whether a Letter of Intent for Supervision is needed before applying. Scholarship applicants must be no older than 40 (doctoral) or 35 (master's) and must not hold another scholarship.

application_steps.title: Complete the online application and upload documents
application_steps.detail: Log in to the university's online system for international students, fill in the form fully and accurately, upload all documents, submit, then pay the RMB 800 fee. The 2027 guide says applications open 5 November 2026 (Beijing time). Deadlines in the guide: 15 December 2026 (first-round CGS through the university), 15 February 2027 (final CGS through the university), 31 March 2027 (Shanghai Government and SJTU Scholarships), 31 May 2027 (self-funded).

application_steps.title: Pick one scholarship channel
application_steps.detail: Apply for scholarships either through the university (select the option in the application system) or through a Chinese embassy or consulate abroad, not both. Through the university, CGS Type B applicants also register in the CGS Information System with SJTU's agency number 10248 and upload SJTU's pre-admission notice, which is issued only after a positive review. Through an embassy, Type A periods vary by country, usually November to April, and you must still complete the SJTU application.

application_steps.title: University assesses documents and sets scholarship levels
application_steps.detail: After the deadline the university assesses documents and decides award levels under the applicable rules. Applicants not nominated for CGS are automatically considered for the Shanghai Government Scholarship and the SJTU Scholarship. Applicants must finish further scholarship procedures by the dates in the university's notices. The guide does not describe interviews or selection criteria.

application_steps.title: Check results in the application system
application_steps.detail: Scholarship results are posted in the application system. The university does not send separate written notifications.

application_steps.title: Receive the Admission Notice and enrol in person
application_steps.detail: Admitted students report to the university in person and complete registration according to the Admission Notice and the new-student guide. Enrolment is scheduled for September 2027. Final-year applicants must give the degree certificate, verification report and final transcripts before enrolment.

application_steps.title: Arrange housing and keep the award through annual review
application_steps.detail: Students may reserve on-campus accommodation or live off campus; allowances follow the award level. Funding periods are not normally extended and all scholarship recipients go through an annual review. CGS review and payment follow the rules of the authorities that run it.

fetch_problems: The scholarship amounts live in the university's online application system, which was not opened.

The programme catalogue PDFs have complex tables; programme names, durations and tuition were read from the text extraction and some columns were interleaved, so only values that were clear are quoted.
The scholarships index page does not mention an SJTU Fellowship; the guide names it for doctoral applicants.
notes: IMPORTANT: the official guide currently online is the 2027 intake guide (applications open 5 November 2026, enrolment September 2027). The stored record is for the 2026 intake (opened 15 October 2025, deadlines 15 December 2025, 15 February 2026, 31 March 2026, 31 May 2026). Editors should decide whether to roll this record to the 2027 intake and update the dates.
Stored data said 'doctoral under 40'; the 2027 guide says 'no older than 40' (master's 'no older than 35').

Stored data said SJTU does not provide free dormitories; the SJTU CGS page says this for undergraduates. The graduate wording in the guide is: the university provides accommodation allowances according to the award level.
The SJTU page numbered 60 is headed as the Shanghai Government Scholarship page in its title but its body describes the Chinese Government Scholarship (Type A and Type B); the body text was used.

Stored programme list for the 2026 catalogue (carried over from stored data) used 2.5-year durations for engineering master's; these were matched against the 2027 catalogue and kept where the 2027 catalogue agrees.
